frequency_question: How often do sovereign states successfully establish operational domestic production lines for advanced imported cruise missiles within a 78-day timeline under wartime constraints?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign state attempting to establish domestic production of a foreign cruise missile system. Excludes standard peacetime transfers, licensed production achieved over multi-year periods (>1 year), and simple depot-level maintenance without manufacturing/assembly capability.

cases.name: Ukraine Neptune domestic serial production setup
Taiwan Hsiung Feng III production scaling
Pakistan Babur cruise missile domestic production establishment
India BrahMos domestic component integration setup

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: Exhaustive set of rapid domestic cruise missile production establishment attempts over the past three decades.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral transfers between advanced states (e.g., Iran/North Korea tech shares) lack public verification of exact timelines, but none are documented under 78 days.
skeleton: Zero historical instances of establishing an advanced cruise missile manufacturing line from scratch within a 78-day timeframe due to immutable physical constraints of tooling, supply chain redirection, facility hardening, and precision calibration.
multiplier: 0 historical instances out of 4 attempted rapid transfers within sub-year windows = 0%
validity_reason: Physical manufacturing lead times, machine tool delivery schedules, and aerospace supply chain bottlenecks remain constrained by immutable physical laws for the foreseeable future.
